title: 72-hour game jam with Claude Code + Blender + three.js: our workflow.
author: katatonicmango
selftext:
For Ludum Dare 60 (theme: Old Tech) we made Moth in the Machine with Opus 5.5. I made a video about it that also plays five other jam entries.

Setup:

\- three.js in the browser, Blender assets, Python scripts to generate them.

\- The first prompt was for roughly 20 minutes of play, Blender assets, good lighting, a tutorial, a story, smooth performance.

What worked:

\- We went with a walking sim in one indoor space, because we knew Claude's limits and the lighting could be set up in a few hours.

\- Python scripts generated the machine, the props and the harbor outside. Blender baked the lighting and three.js brought it into the browser.

What didn't:

\- Parts of the opening story were hard to follow, and some tasks could get stuck if you did things in the wrong order.

\- A bot that could play through to the credits helped with testing, but we still needed human judgment to get a sense of pacing and how intuitive the controls were.

The game on itch.io: https://ldjam.com/events/ludum-dare/60/moth-in-the-machine

Question for anyone who has done a jam with AI tools: where did your tokens go? For us the references and detail pass was the expensive part, not the scaffolding.
